title: Data engineering from contracts to trustworthy retrieval
description: Build an incremental ingestion pipeline with validated schemas, atomic progress, revision-aware state, event-time reasoning and auditable deletion.
review_status: Per-unit Codex AI review status and content-specific evidence in content/reviews.json; no human endorsement claimed.

units.title: Data contracts, SQL constraints and schema evolution
outcomes: Define ownership, revision and compatibility invariants for document events
Demonstrate a schema adapter that accepts two versions without weakening required fields

terms.definition: An agreement about field meaning, shape, identity, ownership and compatibility, not only a JSON shape.
Changing a representation while defining how existing producers, consumers and stored data remain compatible.
An internal form chosen to isolate application logic from source-specific schemas.

narrative: A schema describes representation, while a data contract also describes meaning. An amount needs a currency and unit; a timestamp needs a timezone or a declared interpretation; a document identifier needs an owner and revision scope. An integer-shaped revision of -1 is structurally simple and semantically invalid. Identify required fields, permitted values, length limits, sensitive fields and the authority that assigns each identity before writing an ingestion loop.

Model durable invariants in the database where possible. A composite primary key of owner and document_id prevents one tenant from overwriting another tenant's row with the same local identifier. Foreign keys, unique constraints and check constraints provide guarantees across concurrent writers that a prior application SELECT cannot. A normalized source-of-truth schema supports consistency; a denormalized retrieval projection supports reading. Document which one is authoritative and how the projection can be rebuilt.

Schema changes need an explicit compatibility plan. The fixture accepts schema 1 with name and schema 2 with title, then adapts both to a canonical title. The adapter checks types and required values; it does not blindly rename every field in a payload. In a larger system, deploy consumers that understand both versions before migrating producers, backfill old records, measure old-version traffic and only then remove support. Additive fields may still break strict consumers or change business meaning.

Invalid data requires an intentional policy. Rejecting a whole batch preserves strict completeness but may block healthy records behind one malformed event. Quarantining the event and advancing the source checkpoint can keep the pipeline moving if the quarantine record is durable, traceable and replayable after repair. Report accepted, quarantined, skipped and deleted counts separately. A green process exit is insufficient evidence that every source record reached the index.
practice: Define ownership, revision and compatibility invariants for document events
Demonstrate a schema adapter that accepts two versions without weakening required fields
Add a negative fixture for ambiguous timestamps or currency units
units.debugging: When an index count drops after a schema rollout, compare producer versions, validation reasons and quarantine counts. Re-running the loader without understanding the contract can repeatedly hide the same rejected records.
units.tradeoffs: Strict validation discovers drift early and can stop progress. Tolerant readers reduce coupling but must not silently invent security-sensitive or business-critical values. Make the choice per field and consumer.

worked_examples.title: Worked engineering case
worked_examples.setup: Schema 1 sends name; schema 2 sends title while old events remain in a replay log.
steps: Validate the envelope version before interpreting the fields.
Adapt name or title to one internal representation.
Reject an upsert lacking a meaningful title.
Keep the original event identity and schema metadata for replay and diagnosis.
worked_examples.result: Both supported versions yield a consistent document projection without treating malformed input as an empty valid document.

interviews.question: Is adding a nullable field always a backward-compatible schema change?
interviews.spoken: No. Compatibility depends on validators, serializers, query semantics and the meaning of missing versus null. Test the actual producer/consumer contracts.
interviews.deep:
A strict schema may reject extra fields, a generated client may assume an enum is exhaustive, and a migration may hold locks or rewrite large tables. Use expand/migrate/contract phases and observe consumer behavior before removing the old representation.

Compatibility depends on actual consumers and producers. A nullable added column can break positional SELECT-star unpacking or an old writer with a fixed insert shape. A renamed enum value can parse yet change business meaning. Define schema versions, defaults, nullability and transition rules; use expand/contract changes with old/new readers and writers exercised together.

Database constraints protect identity and relationships while application validation gives useful errors. Neither substitutes for owner-scoped authorization. Parameterize values and preserve source/revision/profile lineage through transformations. Quarantine invalid records with bounded diagnostics and a replay policy; silently coercing a malformed timestamp can corrupt ordering. Run the data contract and CDC fixtures, then show a positive compatible change and an intentionally incompatible consumer. An interview answer should state the migration/backfill/rollback assumptions and expected row outcomes, not merely say that JSON is flexible or SQL is strongly typed.

follow_up.question: Where should tenant identity come from?
follow_up.answer: From a trusted ingestion connection or validated authorization context, not an unchecked field in an arbitrary uploaded document.

units.title: Incremental ingestion, CDC and atomic checkpoints
outcomes: Prove replay after a pre-commit crash creates one projection state
Distinguish source offset, event identity and document revision in a trace

terms.definition: Change data capture: a representation of inserts, updates and deletions from an authoritative source.
Durable progress recording which source position has been handled.
Reapplying the same logical operation does not create another unintended state change.

narrative: An incremental pipeline has two independent facts: what data was written and what source position was acknowledged. If a process writes a document and crashes before saving its cursor, replay is expected. If it advances the cursor before writing and then crashes, the record can be permanently skipped. Put the destination update and progress record in one transaction when they share a database, or use an explicit reconciliation/idempotency protocol across independent systems.

An event ID and a document ID solve different problems. An event ID detects replay of one source change; a document ID identifies the object whose revisions evolve. Hash the original event payload and reject reuse of an event ID with different content. Scope both identities by trusted source or owner. A monotonically increasing document revision prevents a late update from replacing newer state. Do not compare arbitrary version strings lexicographically or assume a wall clock is a safe global ordering.

The fixture uses one source partition with contiguous integer offsets. It rejects a gap, applies the event or records quarantine, then advances the checkpoint inside the same SQLite transaction. A deliberate exception before commit proves that both the projection and checkpoint roll back. A receipt table makes replay at a new source offset recognizable. A production broker needs per-partition cursors and a declared ordering contract; one integer across several independent partitions is not enough.

Exactly-once claims need a boundary. Atomic database progress does not make an external embedding API, object store or search index transactional. Use stable document/revision keys, staging manifests, an outbox or idempotent receiver, and reconcile completed work before promotion. Keep old and new index revisions distinct during a rebuild. Never promote a partial index because a worker merely started or because every task was submitted to a queue.
practice: Prove replay after a pre-commit crash creates one projection state
Distinguish source offset, event identity and document revision in a trace
Explain recovery when the index and checkpoint live in different systems
units.debugging: If records disappear only after restart, inspect whether the source cursor was committed before the destination. If duplicates appear, inspect stable operation keys and receiver behavior; retrying faster does not fix ambiguous commits.
units.tradeoffs: An atomic local transaction is simple when state shares a database. A distributed destination scales independently but introduces partial-failure states that need reconciliation. Neither transport delivery guarantees nor a dedupe flag alone prove the whole application is exactly once.

worked_examples.title: Worked engineering case
worked_examples.setup: Offset 1 updates a policy, then the process crashes immediately before checkpoint commit.
steps: Inject failure after the document write but before transaction completion.
Assert the checkpoint is still 0 and the document table is unchanged.
Replay offset 1 and commit both changes.
Replay it again and observe no second document or external effect.
worked_examples.result: Recovery is demonstrated by durable state, not by counting handler invocations.

interviews.question: Your broker promises exactly-once delivery. Can the consumer charge a customer exactly once?
interviews.spoken: Only if the effect receiver and its identity/reconciliation contract support that end-to-end guarantee. Broker delivery semantics do not atomically commit an independent payment.
interviews.deep:
Use one durable operation key for all attempts, bind it to the payload and owner, persist intent before dispatch, and reconcile uncertain responses against receiver state. An at-least-once consumer can produce one logical effect with receiver deduplication; an exactly-once log can still cause duplicate external effects.

A broker's delivery guarantee does not atomically include an external database or payment API. In a single database sink, commit the destination mutation, exact-event deduplication record and checkpoint together. A crash after commit but before acknowledgment then produces a safe duplicate delivery. Compare canonical material payload, not only operation key and offset.

The rollout contract rejects changed-payload replay at the same offset, gaps and unapproved tombstone restoration. Its checkpoint trigger fault proves that earlier document and consumed-event writes roll back. Owner belongs in every relevant key and query. For a remote effect, use receiver idempotency or reconciliation under the same business identity and document retention/uncertainty limits. Fresh UUIDs on retry defeat logical deduplication. A credible interview defense traces both the local transaction and the first external boundary that cannot participate in it, then predicts each crash point's committed state independently.

follow_up.question: What if the receiver has no idempotency or lookup capability?
follow_up.answer: The uncertainty cannot be eliminated by a local transaction. Require a manual reconciliation or redesign the effect boundary.

incident.symptom: A restart loses one policy update even though ingestion previously logged success.
incident.evidence: Compare source offset, destination revision, event receipt, transaction boundary and quarantine record from an isolated fixture.
incident.investigation: Inject failure between destination mutation and cursor persistence. A cursor-first implementation skips work; a write-first implementation without dedupe can repeat work.
incident.recovery: Rebuild/reconcile the affected revision from authoritative source state using the original operation identity, then resume only from verified progress.
incident.prevention: Commit local projection and checkpoint atomically, retain payload-bound event identities and test every crash boundary.

units.title: Event time, late data, windows and backpressure
outcomes: Assign late records to event-time windows with a declared correction policy
Show why document revision order differs from arrival order

terms.definition: When the event occurred in its source domain, as distinct from when a consumer processed it.
A progress estimate used to decide when a system expects most earlier events to have arrived.
A policy describing how late events can revise or bypass an already emitted window result.

narrative: A streaming record can arrive late because a device buffered it, a network partition healed or a backfill replayed historical events. Event time describes the source event; processing time describes the worker's current clock. A five-minute event-time sales total answers a different question from the number of events processed in the last five minutes. Store enough provenance to distinguish them and validate timezones before grouping.

Window boundaries and late-data policy are part of the result contract. In a fixed five-minute window, an event at 12:04 belongs before the 12:05 boundary even if it arrives at 12:09. A watermark helps a system emit results without waiting forever; it is not a physical proof that no earlier event can ever arrive. Decide whether a late record updates a prior result, enters a correction stream or goes to review. Consumers need update/retraction semantics if totals can change.

Order also matters outside aggregation. The fixture receives a document revision 3 and then revision 2; its version predicate preserves revision 3 while retaining evidence that the later-arriving event was processed. Revision order is not the same thing as event-time windowing. Extend the lab with two partitions and show how a slow partition changes a global watermark estimate. Write down the assumption that makes each comparison meaningful.

Backpressure prevents a temporary slowdown from becoming an out-of-memory failure. Bound queue length and in-flight work, then choose whether a full admission queue blocks, rejects, sheds optional work or persists a retryable task. Track queue age as well as queue size: ten jobs may be harmless at one millisecond each and disastrous at a minute each. Adding workers can overwhelm an already saturated database, so measure the downstream bottleneck before increasing concurrency.
practice: Assign late records to event-time windows with a declared correction policy
Show why document revision order differs from arrival order
Define bounded admission and overload behavior for an ingestion service
units.debugging: A sudden daily total change may be a correct late-data correction rather than corruption. Compare event time, arrival time, source partition and revision before deleting records or changing the watermark policy.
units.tradeoffs: Waiting longer improves completeness at the cost of result latency and retained state. Fast preliminary results are useful if they are labeled provisional and can be corrected. Dropping late events simplifies storage but biases aggregates unless measured.

worked_examples.title: Worked engineering case
worked_examples.setup: A 12:04 purchase arrives at 12:09 after a 12:00–12:05 summary was emitted.
steps: Preserve both event and arrival timestamps.
Emit a correction or route to review, recording that this is not a new 12:05–12:10 purchase.
worked_examples.result: The aggregate remains interpretable and consumers understand whether earlier totals can change.

interviews.question: Does a watermark guarantee that all older events have arrived?
interviews.spoken: No. It represents a system progress assumption or estimate. You still need an explicit policy for late or corrected data.
interviews.deep:
A source can reconnect with buffered events or a repair can replay history. The correctness contract includes window assignment, triggering, allowed lateness, duplicate handling and update/retraction behavior. Test an out-of-order sequence rather than relying only on an ordered happy path.

A watermark expresses an estimate of event-time progress under the runner's assumptions. Delayed sources, disconnections and clock errors can still deliver older events. Define allowed lateness, windows, triggers and whether outputs are append-only changes or upserts/corrections. Processing time is when the pipeline handled data; it is not the business event time.

An early result followed by a late correction can double a downstream total if the consumer treats both as independent inserts. Carry stable window/entity/revision identity and make replacement semantics explicit. Use bounded queues/backpressure so sink slowdown cannot grow memory indefinitely. The local data fixture and optional real Beam lab provide different levels of evidence; label runner, version and observed outputs. Assess schema failures, nulls, duplicates, freshness and owner leakage separately. The learner must reproduce a late correction and explain the expected sink state, not merely repeat that streaming is faster than batch.

follow_up.question: Would increasing worker concurrency fix old queue age?
follow_up.answer: Only if workers are the bottleneck. A saturated downstream service may become slower or fail more often under extra concurrency.

units.title: Lineage, deletion, data quality and safe index promotion
outcomes: Trace one indexed passage to its source revision and processing configuration
Prove a tombstone survives replay of an older update

terms.definition: A record of the source revisions and transformations that produced an artifact.
A durable deletion marker that prevents an older replay from resurrecting deleted state.
Comparing independent state records and correcting missing, duplicated or stale artifacts.

narrative: A useful retrieval artifact needs more than text and a vector. Record source identity, owner/ACL scope, source revision, parsing configuration, chunking configuration, embedding model/version and build identity. Without this lineage, a quality regression after deployment cannot be separated from a changed source document. Preserve page/section or character-span provenance so a citation can be checked against the actual source revision.

Deletion is a distributed data problem. Removing the source row does not automatically remove embeddings, search caches, generated summaries, exports or retained traces. The fixture uses a revisioned tombstone so a delayed older upsert cannot revive the document. In a real service, enumerate derived stores, enqueue deletion or invalidation, track completion and prevent a stale backfill from republishing removed content. Retention policy should distinguish deletion of source material from minimum audit evidence.

Data-quality checks need denominators and slices. Track expected source records, accepted records, rejected records, duplicate events, deleted objects and visible indexed revisions. An unchanged total count can hide replacement of one tenant's documents with another's. Reconcile identities and revision hashes, sample citation spans and measure retrieval changes on a fixed gold set. A single aggregate success percentage rarely diagnoses the actual defect.

Build a replacement index in staging and promote an immutable manifest only after completeness, authorization and quality checks pass. Keep the previous manifest long enough for an intentional rollback, subject to deletion and privacy rules. A rollback cannot legitimately restore material that has since been revoked. Rebuilding from authoritative data should reproduce the permitted projection; document any nondeterminism from external parsers or model versions.
practice: Trace one indexed passage to its source revision and processing configuration
Prove a tombstone survives replay of an older update
Define independent completeness and authorization checks before index promotion
units.debugging: When deleted text remains visible, query each derived store and cache by source identity and revision. Clearing a browser cache only hides one symptom if the search index still serves the passage.
units.tradeoffs: Keeping full provenance improves diagnosis and uses storage. Storing unrestricted raw documents in every log or artifact creates privacy risk. Keep the minimal authorized evidence needed for reproducibility and define retention/access rules.

worked_examples.title: Worked engineering case
worked_examples.setup: Revision 4 deletes a policy; a historical backfill later replays revision 2.
steps: Persist a deletion marker at revision 4.
Reject or ignore the older projection update while retaining the event receipt.
Invalidate active index entries and check each derived store.
Require the next promoted manifest to exclude the deleted policy.
worked_examples.result: Replay does not resurrect the document, and the deletion has observable completion evidence.

interviews.question: How do you prove an index rebuild is safe to promote?
interviews.spoken: Compare an immutable build manifest with expected identities and revisions, test tenant isolation and evaluate fixed quality slices before switching readers.
interviews.deep:
A job-success flag measures execution, not coverage. Check skipped/quarantined inputs, revoked sources, parser/embedding versions and citation provenance. Promote the tested manifest atomically and keep an authorized rollback route.

A rebuild needs a declared source snapshot, transformation/embedding profile and catch-up position. Validate counts, values, scope, revisions and independent relevance cases before switching readers; matching row counts alone can conceal swapped owners or missing exception text. Publish an immutable generation or atomic pointer rather than exposing partially built state.

Deletion intent remains authoritative while rebuild and restore occur. A restored backup may contain documents deleted after the snapshot, so replay revocation/tombstone events before serving traffic and verify caches/projections too. The restore drill demonstrates a bounded local copy and deletion replay, not full service RTO or physical erasure. Deliver source/profile hashes, eligible output IDs, negative results and a rollback/cutover plan. An interview defense distinguishes logical exclusion, physical cleanup, backup retention and historical access, instead of declaring deletion complete because one SQL row disappeared.

follow_up.question: Can you roll back to any older index?
follow_up.answer: No. The rollback must still enforce current deletions, ACLs and retention rules.
